Subject: Post-demo: Structured output guardrails + retry strategy

Hi Elena / Dev team —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have a concrete plan for the evaluation:

What we covered (summary)
- Target flow: intake -> model -> downstream billing service via HTTP function call -> persist structured payload (JSON).
- Key success criteria you called out: 1) strict JSON schema conformance, 2) >=98% field-level accuracy for extracted entities, 3) <200ms p95 inference latency for short requests (<=256 tokens).

Redwood recommendations for initial eval
- Models to try: rw-open-13b-ft (fp16) for cost/latency baseline, and rw-large-70b-fp16 for final quality checks. We’ll run both with the same prompt set.
- Quantization profile: q4_0 for the 13B baseline; run 70B in fp16 on dedicated capacity for the quality pass.
- Structured output check: we attached a starting JSON schema (structured-output-spec-v1.json) — we’ll validate each response against it and report per-field failures.

Tool/function calling and retry guidance
- Function calling: prefer explicit function_call interface (model returns function name + typed args) instead of parsing free text. That makes downstream idempotency simpler.
- Retries: use exponential backoff with jitter for transient 5xx from downstream systems (max 3 attempts). Include an idempotency key in the function payload to avoid duplicate side-effects. If function fails after retries, fall back to "human-in-the-loop" queue with the original payload.

Deliverables we’ll provide
- A sample prompt set + canonical expected outputs (Drive link below).
- Per-model benchmark CSV with latency/throughput/schema-conformance columns.
- Quick-run harness (script) that hits your staging endpoint with function_call enabled.

Next steps / ask of you
- Please confirm preferred evaluation window (we proposed Tue 8/24 09:00-13:00 PDT).
- Share an example downstream schema or a staging URL for the function call if available.
- Any security/compliance requirements we should include before running (SOC2 evidence, IP allowlist, encryption at rest)?

Elena — quick technical notes to address the items above and make the eval actionable.

SOC2 / KMS
- We’ll provide a SOC2 evidence packet (redacted) and a short KMS integration doc for key wrapping in Private deployments. I’ll upload the checklist to the Drive folder by EOD 8/24.

Tracing / auditability
- Our harness will emit a trace_id (uuid) for each request. Trace_id is propagated to the function_call payload and logged on the backend CSV. That will let you correlate model -> function -> downstream response.
- We’ll include the raw model output column in the CSV (base64-safe sanitized snippet) and a separate column with JSON-schema validation errors (property path + failure reason).

Schema validation specifics
- We validate against JSON Schema draft-07 with two passes: strict parse (type/coercion) then semantic checks (date formats, currency codes). Failure rows include path and error code (e.g., required_missing, type_mismatch, pattern_mismatch).

Retries / idempotency
- Recommended implementation: client generates idempotency_key at request creation (UUID v4). If downstream returns 502/503/504, client does exponential backoff 500ms -> 1s -> 2s and retries (max 3). On each retry we include the same idempotency_key. Our harness can run with that behavior toggled on/off.
- If retries exhausted, the payload is moved to a human-review queue with the trace_id and raw model output attached.

Benchmarks
- Attached a quick CSV with the baseline run we did in staging (benchmarks-skyline-20270821.csv). NOTE: those runs used the q4_0 profile for the 13B; expect slightly better latency with a tuned batch size in your environment.

Let me know if you want us to include an automatic fallback policy in the runtime: e.g., if JSON schema conformance <95% on a rolling window, route to a higher-capacity model variant for a canary period.

— Rishi
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Acceptance & quality regression policy
- Primary metric: JSON schema conformance (strict) — target >=98% for baseline.
- Secondary: field-level accuracy (entity matching) — we’ll compute F1 per field using your annotated sample set.
- Regression monitoring: if conformance drops >5% vs baseline during rollout, Redwood will auto-route 10% of traffic to the higher-capacity variant and flag the CS/Dev team in Slack.

Next steps for you
- Confirm any schema relaxations by EOD 8/24.
- Share a staging endpoint for function_call by 8/24 12:00 PDT so Marissa can wire the harness.

We’ll follow up with the SOC2 upload and the harness link. If that all looks good I’ll send calendar invites for the Thu quality pass.
